messages:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert: multiple containers in gpu-pool-3 are restarting due to OOM/CUDA errors. Automated rollback triggered for recent runtime change. Paging oncall. link: https://metrics.redwood.example/incident/1778001234 :rotating_light:
anya (oncall): ack — I'm on it, pulling logs + checking node health.
anya (oncall): initial customer impact: 2% 5xx spike for hosted text-gen, tail latency up ~800ms for some regions. Not full outage but elevated errors.
max (eng-runtime): seeing repeated `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` from paged-attn allocator on hosts gpu-3a/gpu-3b. Heap trending up slowly over 2 days on those hosts.
leo (sre): confirmed node flaps: kube reports crashloop backoffs on node gpu-3b; restarting container sometimes recovers for ~30-45m then it creeps again.
jessica (eng-oncall): logs snippet: ```
2026-03-14T02:13:44Z runtime[pid=2241]: Allocator: paged-attn slab alloc failed, trying remap
2026-03-14T02:13:44Z runtime[pid=2241]: CUDA ERROR: out of memory (driver=510.XX)
2026-03-14T02:13:44Z runtime[pid=2241]: kv_cache resident_pages=524288 -> 536974 (+12686)
```
max (eng-runtime): that delta looks like slow resident page accumulation — fragmentation/slow leak in slab bitmap for KV cache. It's not a single big allocation, it's micro-fragmentation plus small leaks when pages are pinned.
anya (oncall): quick mitigation plan: 1) Drain gpu-3b from serving pool (migrate active rays) 2) Force restart runtime on gpu-3a/gpu-3b to free resident pages 3) Temporarily lower max_sequence / batch_size for hosts in region to reduce KV pressure 4) Enable aggressive eviction profile (evict threshold -> 0.6)
matt (infra): draining gpu-3b now: `kubectl cordon gpu-3b && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data gpu-3b` — will move live pods.
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident PD-78541 created, severity SEV2, oncall rota notified.
customer-ops: Notifying CS for customers with high qps in region-eu, short note drafted.
leo (sre): after draining, we saw immediate drop in OOM errors on control plane for that node. However gpu-3a still creeping. Restarting runtime on gpu-3a now.
anya (oncall): applied eviction policy bump on cluster: `redwood-cli config set allocator.eviction_threshold=0.6 --cluster=eu-prod` — watching telemetry.
max (eng-runtime): adding temporary hotfix that forces periodic slab bitmap compaction every 30m — it's a blunt instrument but should help fragmentation while we root cause. Pushing canary to one node.
jessica (eng-oncall): can we also reduce `prefix_cache_ttl` to force earlier eviction? customers with long chats will be impacted but better than OOM.
max (eng-runtime): yes reducing `prefix_cache_ttl` to 900s on canary. Doing now.
anya (oncall): telemetry update: memory climb rate on remaining nodes dropped from +12k pages / 10m to +2.5k pages / 10m after eviction + restart. 5xx rate stabilized but tail latency still 300ms above baseline.
leo (sre): customer-impact summary for page: approx 8 customers saw intermittent request failures in EU region during the peak window (02:10–02:40). No persisted data loss.
matt (infra): note — observed a deprecated kernel driver message on gpu-3a earlier, driver upgrade patch queued; avoid rolling drivers in-prod during incident.
max (eng-runtime): root cause hypothesis: paged-attn allocator's slab free path misses a small class of pinned KV pages when attention paging rebinds pages. Leads to slow resident growth + fragmentation, eventually OOM on long-lived hosts.
anya (oncall): next steps: 1) keep hotfix compaction running cluster-wide for 6 hours 2) schedule targeted restart window for remaining affected nodes during low traffic 3) open a runtime bug with reproducer and perf traces (assign to eng-runtime)
max (eng-runtime): creating issue RUN-1259 with initial traces and instructions to reproduce under high prefix churn. @eng-runtime please triage after incident.
jessica (eng-oncall): handing off to night oncall @mike (tomorrow) — I'll leave runbook notes in incident doc. Current owner: max for code fix, anya for mitigation until nodes stabilized.
matt (infra): started rolling restarts of remaining 3 nodes in pool with 5m stagger. I'll keep an eye on pod restarts.
leo (sre): monitoring: setting up alert to catch resident_pages delta > 5k per 10m and auto-snoop slab state to S3 for debugging.
anya (oncall): incident update to status page: partial degradations in EU text-gen; mitigations in place; no ongoing outage. Drafting message.
customer-ops: Sent customers in impacted list a short note: "We experienced elevated errors and latency in EU between 02:10–02:40 UTC. Mitigations applied, root cause under investigation. We will follow up with more details."
max (eng-runtime): quick workaround landed in canary, will promote after 30m of clean metrics. If regressions appear, will rollback.
analysis: the failure chain: slow KV page pin -> slab fragmentation -> gradual resident growth -> CUDA OOM on allocation -> container crash -> node flap -> service errors. Not a sudden leak but persistent micro-accumulation.
jessica (eng-oncall): thanks team. If no more flares in next 60m, I'll transition this to post-incident follow-up. max please include timeline and patch in the ticket.
pagerduty-bot: PD-78541 updated: status -> acknowledged; next: mitigation in progress.
anya (oncall): confirming: last_message. I'll update oncall handoff notes and link to RUN-1259.
max (eng-runtime): adding final note: long-term fixes: ensure allocator free path validates page ownership on rebinding, add regression tests simulating high-prefix churn, and consider adaptive eviction that responds to slab fragmentation signals.
jessica (eng-oncall): handoff complete to night shift. Closing thread for live triage. :white_check_mark:
